note: Baseline tokens (millions) and hours are for size M. Replace with your own delivery actuals to calibrate.

intent.name: Intent Compiler
checks: Every requirement traces to the brief
Nothing above 0.35 ambiguity ships without a question
intent.done: Every requirement has an owning node and a test stub.
intent.does: Reads the brief and source material, splits it into atomic testable requirements, scores ambiguity and drafts the questions for scope sign-off.

test_strategy.name: Test Strategist
checks: Every requirement covered by a scenario
Mutation check that scenarios can fail
test_strategy.done: Coverage matrix is complete before code is written.
test_strategy.does: Turns every requirement into acceptance scenarios and contract tests before any code exists, and generates synthetic test data.

domain_model.name: Domain Modeler
domain_model.done: All must-support elements mapped and validated.
domain_model.does: Maps the domain to standards and the existing data model: entities, profiles, value sets and data dictionaries.

architecture.name: Solution Architect
checks: Every requirement mapped to a component
architecture.done: Contracts compile into server and client stubs.
architecture.does: Designs the solution: records decisions as ADRs, writes API contracts and sequence flows, and builds the threat model later nodes must honour.

data_migration.name: Data & Migration
checks: Up and down migration on a production-shaped snapshot
data_migration.does: Writes schema changes and reversible migrations, rehearses them on production-shaped data, and seeds reference data.

backend.name: Backend Builder
backend.done: Service passes contract tests in staging.
backend.does: Implements services, APIs, jobs and business logic against the frozen contracts, with unit and contract tests.

integration.name: Integration Builder
integration.done: All synthetic cases complete end to end.
integration.does: Builds connectors to external systems with retries, idempotency and failure handling, proven against partner sandboxes.

ui.name: UI Builder
ui.done: All UI scenarios green on the contract mock.
ui.does: Builds screens and flows from the design system, wired to the contract mock, with accessibility and end-to-end tests.

workflow.name: Workflow & Rules Builder
workflow.done: Every rule has a passing positive and negative test.
workflow.does: Encodes business rules, eligibility logic, state machines, timers and notifications as testable decision tables.

ai_ml.name: AI Component Builder
ai_ml.done: Eval scores meet the agreed threshold.
ai_ml.does: Builds the AI component (prompts, models, pipelines) together with a golden-set eval suite and safety checks.

infra.name: Infrastructure Builder
infra.does: Writes infrastructure as code for environments, networking, secrets and tenancy, checked against policy.

reporting.name: Reporting Builder
reporting.done: Every metric reconciles to source data.
reporting.does: Builds dashboards, metrics and exports, reconciling every figure to source data.

test_runner.name: Test Runner & Fixer
checks: Fix loop capped at 4 cycles, then escalates
test_runner.done: All scenarios pass twice in a row.
test_runner.does: Runs the full acceptance suite, diagnoses failures, fixes them in a capped loop and escalates what it cannot fix.

security.name: Security Scanner
security.done: Zero high or critical findings open.
security.does: Scans code, dependencies, secrets and logs, and blocks release on high or critical findings.

compliance.name: Compliance Checker
compliance.done: All compliance controls have passing evidence.
compliance.does: Checks each regulated control against evidence from the build and flags gaps before review.

performance.name: Performance Tester
checks: p95 latency and error rate under target
performance.done: Load targets met at expected peak.
performance.does: Load-tests the staging build at expected peak and reports latency and error rates against targets.

release.name: Release Agent
release.does: Prepares the production rollout: canary stages, feature flags and a rollback runbook, and rehearses the rollback.

evidence.name: Evidence Bundler
evidence.does: Collects every test result, scan and approval into a signed requirement-to-evidence pack for audit.

scope.name: Scope sign-off
scope.why: A scope error multiplies cost in every node downstream.

arch.name: Architecture review
arch.why: Contracts fan out to parallel builders. Changing them later restarts them all.

dba.name: Schema change approval
dba.why: Schema changes are the hardest step to undo in production.

ux.name: UX review
ux.why: Low risk, so it auto-passes at Balanced autonomy or higher.

model.name: Model evaluation review
model.approve: Eval thresholds met and failure modes accepted.
model.why: AI output quality cannot be judged from code review alone.

review.name: Risk-routed code review
review.approve: High-risk diffs approved; the rest accepted on evidence.
review.why: Spends senior attention only where a bug would be expensive.

golive.name: Go-live approval
golive.approve: Evidence complete and canary plan accepted.
golive.why: Production release is irreversible for users who see it.

examples.sample: Providers need to see where each prior authorization stands without calling the payer. Submit PA requests from the portal using FHIR PAS, track status live, fall back to X12 278 for payers without FHIR, and keep an audit trail that meets HIPAA and CMS-0057-F decision timelines.
examples.idr: Build the dispute intake module for a No Surprises Act IDR platform. Billing teams upload batches of out-of-network claims (CSV or 837). The system checks federal IDR eligibility (open negotiation period expired, qualified item or service, 4-business-day initiation window), groups batchable claims, drafts the IDR initiation notice, and submits it to the federal IDR portal. Multi-tenant with tenant-level isolation and SOC 2 controls. Use AI to extract claim details from uploaded EOB PDFs. Include a dashboard of disputes by deadline and status.
